head: claude/mi171-alpaca-overclose-population
title: MI-171: the Alpaca over-close population, counted — 1 of 12 pairs, 0 events, and one loaded gun
body:
**Session** `session_019G7vh8rkRZryXJGhbhfov7` · registered `pending-20260907T214605Z` · **Tier 1**, self-landing (`state=declared_self_land`).

`BL-20260907-ALPACA-CLOSE-OF-ONE-TRADE-LIQUIDATES-ITS-SIBLINGS` ends with a `Population note` that says **"We did not look."** This PR looks. Verdict: `docs/research/alpaca-over-close-population-2026-09-07.md`.

---

## Part 1 — PR #11271 is unblocked and GREEN

**It was a false positive, and I confirmed that myself rather than taking it on report.**

- `risk_pct` is a **configured parameter**, not a statistic over any population: `alpaca_live.risk.risk_pct: 0.02` is a field at `config/accounts.yaml:1111` (operator-directed 2026-08-29), read by `src/research/risk_basis.py:142` — *"Read the account's declared `risk.risk_pct` from accounts.yaml."*
- The table already states its population one sentence above it — *"Measured on row 5415's own numbers"* — **n=1 by construction**, since it reconstructs one specific sizing decision.

**Your end-of-row instruction is correct, and I verified the rendering with cmark-gfm — the renderer GitHub itself uses — rather than reasoning about it.** Own-line truncates the table to 2 of 5 rows and spills the rest as a paragraph; end-of-row renders **byte-identically to the unmarked baseline** (GFM ignores a cell in excess of the header's column count). Rendering the whole document before and after gives identical HTML: 7 tables, 45 rows both ways.

⚠️ Worth recording: **`mistune` breaks the table in BOTH placements** and would have talked me out of the correct fix. It is not GFM-compliant on excess cells. Don't use it as the oracle here.

**I pushed the one-line fix to `mi140-alpaca-live-refusal-verdict` itself** (as myself — my session has never held the manager lease; verified against all 59 revisions of `MANAGER-LEASE.json`), rather than superseding #11271 from my own branch. That is what makes **#11271 itself** go green: all 4 checks now `success`, `guards` included, at head `9016dc7c`. Nothing else in the document is touched.

---

## Part 2 — the count nobody had made

**Population for every figure below: the 1000 rows `/api/diag/journal?table=trades` returns** — ids 4544–5543, `2026-08-10T15:00:59Z` → `2026-09-07T21:02:20Z` (28.2 days). 573 `closed` · 370 `rejected` · 30 `exchange_rejected` · 27 `open`; **600** rows ever held a venue position. Alpaca's share across all four Alpaca accounts: **171 rows** (32 closed, 13 open, 125 rejected, 1 exchange_rejected).

### (a) 1 of 12 multi-row pairs is Alpaca

`alpaca_portfolio` / **TLT**. The other 11 are `bybit_1` (6), `bybit_2` (2), `bybit_portfolio` (2), `ib_paper` MGC (1). `bybit_2` appears with BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT exactly as MI-167 recorded.

### (b) 0 over-close events — we looked and found none

Measured two independent ways, each with its positive control:

| measurement | result | positive control on the same probe |
|---|---|---|
| Alpaca closes that fired while a sibling row on the same `(account, symbol)` was open | **0 of 32** | the identical scan returns **187** on Bybit — and MI-167 independently reported **187**, an exact agreement I did not tune for |
| open Alpaca rows with no venue position behind them | **0 of 13** | the same diff finds **3** venue positions with no journal row, so it detects divergence both ways |

Every one of the 13 open Alpaca rows is backed with journal quantity equal to venue quantity **exactly**. **The zero is not "the path is cold"** — 32 Alpaca closes fired; none coincided with an open sibling.

This is also the `journal-open vs exchange_positions` diff MI-167's pass-3 item 2 asked for and did not build ("it would have found this in one call"). Built, read-only, committed.

---

## Three things you did not ask for, one of which changes the picture

### 1. ⚠️ The precondition is live on Alpaca RIGHT NOW

`alpaca_portfolio` / TLT holds **two simultaneously-open rows at this moment**: row 5266 (16 shares, since 08-31) and row 5414 (56 shares, since 09-03). Venue: TLT short **72.0** — their exact sum, both fully backed.

**The next close of either row flattens all 72 shares and leaves the other row open with nothing behind it.** The zero in (b) is a statement about the past. I confirmed the mechanism first-hand, not from the row: `AlpacaClient.close(self, symbol: str)` (`alpaca_client.py:859`) **accepts no quantity at all**, and `execute.py:2964` calls `exchange_client.close(symbol)` where the IB branch two lines up calls `close(symbol, direction, qty)`. The comment there says it outright — *"the qty argument is informational here"*.

`alpaca_portfolio` is `class: paper`, so no real money is at stake **today**. But it is the same client and the same path `alpaca_live` inherits the moment MI-140 is remediated. **This pair is the proof that the precondition occurs in practice, not merely in principle.**

### 2. The backlog row's 13 is off by one, for a findable reason

I re-derived and get **12**. The count is **stable at 12** across start-field (`timestamp`/`created_at`) and boundary-convention variations. It becomes 13 under exactly one change: **counting `exchange_rejected` rows as having held a position** — which adds `alpaca_paper`/GLD on row 5347. An exchange-rejected row never got shares, so it can be neither victim nor cause; **12 is the count that answers the question.**

Two things I cannot rule out, stated rather than glossed: the window has slid 4 rows since MI-167 read it (theirs 4540–5539, mine 4544–5543) and ids 4540–4543 are unreachable; and I have not read MI-167's script, only its prose. What makes the `exchange_rejected` explanation more than a guess is that it reproduces **13 pairs AND 2 Alpaca pairs** simultaneously and exactly, which the roll-off hypothesis does not predict at all. Graded **INFERRED** on MEASURED inputs. **Either way the answer to your question is unchanged**: 1 of 12 strict, 2 of 13 loose — a small minority both ways.

### 3. MI-167's blast-radius table is account-scoped where the defect is client-scoped

It graded **`alpaca_live` alone**. There are **four** Alpaca accounts and **all four share `alpaca_client.py`**, so all four are exposed by code — and unlike `alpaca_live`, three of them actually trade. **The one pair that reached the precondition is on `alpaca_portfolio`, which that table does not list.** MI-167's conclusion about *real money* stands untouched; its coverage of the *code path* does not.

---

## The read I could NOT make

⚠️ **`GET /api/diag/journal` takes only `table` and `limit`, and `limit` is clamped to 1000** (`src/web/api/routers/diag.py:1541`, `:860`). **No `offset`, no `since`** — unlike `/audit_query` in the same file, which has both. Verified rather than inferred: asking for `limit=3000` returns the same 1000 rows.

**So MI-167's "28-day window" is the shape of a cap, not a chosen window, and no figure in this PR is an all-time count.** MI-167's pass-3 item 3 asks for incidence "across all accounts and all time"; for the `trades` table that read is **not available** through the diag surface as it stands.

Consequently **3 venue positions are reported as UNGRADEABLE, not as clean**: `alpaca_paper` IEF (short 141) and `alpaca_portfolio` IEF (short 152) have **zero journal rows of any status** inside the cap, and `alpaca_paper` SPY (long 11) has 4 rows all `rejected`. Whatever opened them is outside the cap. They may be ordinary long-held positions whose opening rows rolled off. I am not grading them on inference.

## Scope kept

- **No close path touched.** `AlpacaClient.close` and `execute.close_open_position` are quoted, never modified — Tier-3, MI-168's PR #11279, blocked on two operator decisions. This is a measurement, not a fix.
- **I did not apply MI-167's remedy to Alpaca.** Its confirmation and its operation are both symbol-scoped, so they already agree; narrowing the confirmation would re-introduce `BL-20260707-ALPACA-CLOSE-NOT-CONFIRMED-FLAT`'s false-SUCCESS on a real-money-capable path. My read of both call sites agrees with the row.
- No `src/`, no `config/`, no `deploy/`, no workflows. The live reads were GETs.

## Verification

`python3 scripts/ci/run_guards.py --base main` → **PASS 71 · FAIL 0 · SKIP 19**.

Honest note on how that number was reached: 4 guards initially failed for **missing tools in my container**, not defects — `pytest` and `lint-imports` were both absent, and `pytest` being absent also made my first baseline-against-`main` reading of two of them ("pre-existing") wrong. I installed both and re-ran rather than reporting them unrun. Four guards then caught **real** defects in my own work, all fixed rather than suppressed: `ruff` F541, `diagnostic-provenance` C (an unquantified universal claim), `unwired-artifact` (declared `# wiring: manual-only` with the actual reason), and `check_backlog_refs` — where two **line-wrapped backlog ids** were resolving to nothing, exactly the truncated-id shape the rules doc's verification ledger names. `pr-landing-guard` → `state=declared_self_land`.

Also asserted inside the transform, per RULE ONE: **one of my own assertions caught me claiming 14 open Alpaca rows when there are 13.**

## Reproducing it

Inputs are committed, so nothing here depends on live access:

```
python3 scripts/research/mi171_alpaca_overclose_population.py
```

reading `docs/research/artifacts/mi171-alpaca-overclose/` (`trades-4544-5543.json.gz`, `alpaca-exchange-positions.json`). Live reads were taken with `scripts/ops/diag_fetch.sh` direct over `https://ict-bot.duckdns.org`, exit 0, not via the issue relay.

## ⚠️ The board START could not be posted, by any path

Recorded rather than skipped. **Both routes are blocked:**

1. MCP `add_issue_comment` on #6927 → **write-scope 403** (`Resource not accessible by integration`). Distinguished from the transient drop as instructed: `issue_read method=get_comments` on the same object succeeded immediately before and after, and two write attempts were refused with no backoff clearing it.
2. The `board-post.yml` relay (fresh filename `mi171-start-20260907T2200Z.md`, on the separate branch `claude/mi171-board-start` so its bot commit could not strand this PR's CI) → the run recorded **`FAILED: GraphQL: Commenting is disabled on issues with more than 2500 comments (addComment)`**.

That is an independent confirmation of the already-open `BL-20260907-COORDINATION-BOARD-6927-IS-FULL-SO-THE-MANDATORY-START-POST-IS-IMPOSSIBLE-BY-EVERY-PATH`. **The relay behaved correctly** — it failed loudly and wrote `FAILED:` to its result file, which is exactly the contract. The claim text is preserved on that branch. `claude/mi171-board-start` carries nothing else and is yours to delete.

**This PR was also opened through a relay** (`pr-opener.yml`), because `create_pull_request` returned the same write-scope 403 twice. Opened ready, not draft, per the 2026-09-03 ruling.

## How this PR got opened, and three branches you may want to delete

I did **not** open it with `create_pull_request` — that returned a write-scope 403 twice, so this PR came through the `pr-opener.yml` relay. An earlier attempt became **#11289**, opened by `claude-pr-automerge` off my `.github/pr-automerge-requests/` file, which sets `title` to the head-commit subject and a hardcoded boilerplate body. It was therefore titled *"MI-171: unwrap two backlog ids so they resolve"* — the subject of a small follow-up commit, and a real misrepresentation of the change. `update_pull_request` 403s for me too, so neither field could be edited in place. **#11289 was closed via the `pr-close.yml` relay and replaced by this PR: same branch, same head `79dddf2c`, nothing discarded — only the title and body differ.**

Three throwaway branches carry only relay requests and are yours to delete: `claude/mi171-board-start` (the failed board post), `claude/mi171-pr-request` (a `pr-opener` request that correctly no-op'd against #11289) and `claude/mi171-pr-fix` (the close request).

## For the manager's register

My row `WO-20260907-UNBLOCK-11271-S-ONE-STATED-POPULATION-FALSE` is complete as scoped. Two scope notes for `SESSIONS.json`, which you own: Part 1 landed on `mi140-alpaca-live-refusal-verdict` (i.e. into **#11271**) rather than on my own branch, so the unit touches two PRs; and finding 3 above means the Alpaca exposure surface is **four accounts, not one**, which may matter to how MI-168's row and MI-140's coupling are scoped.
